sentences.text: This bail application is filed under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.48 of 2024 of Thottilpalam Police Station, Kozhikode, which is now stated to be pending as S.C. No.431 of 2024 before the Fast Track Special Court, Nadapuram,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 354A, 354A(1)(i), 354(i)(iii), 354B,
376(2)(f) and 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, apart from Sections 5(I), 5(m) and 5(n) r/w Section 6(1) and Sections 9(I), 9(m) and 9(n) r/w Section 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The prosecution alleges that the accused had, from July 2023 to 28.01.2024 repeatedly committed penetrative sexual assault on a victim who is his relative and only 9 years in age and even showed her obscene videos and thereby committed the offences alleged.
Petitioner was arrested on 01.02.2024 and he has been in custody since then.
4. Heard Sri. B. Krishna Mani, the learned counsel for the 2025:KER:37231 petitioner as well as Smt. Maya M. N., the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. On an earlier occasion, petitioner had approached this Court in B.A. No.9248 of 2024.

However,
petitioner withdrew the said bail application seeking liberty to approach the trial court after some time if the trial is not concluded immediately.
Pursuant to the aforesaid liberty, petitioner filed a bail application before the trial court as C.M.P. No.40 of 2025.
However, by order dated 11.02.2025, the said bail application was dismissed after noticing the grave and heinous crime allegedly committed by the petitioner.
It was also noticed that no change of circumstances had arisen in the case to grant bail to the petitioner, and also that the case was posted for examination of the prosecution witnesses.
The learned Public Prosecutor pointed out that trial has already commenced and almost all the prosecution witnesses have been examined.

Bearing in mind the circumstance that the trial has already commenced as well as the nature of allegations against the petitioner and the young age of the minor victim, I am of the view that this is not a fit case where petitioner could be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is dismissed.
Balan.
